lanes.summary: There's no AI consent step and no AI toggle in Settings. The privacy notice names no AI provider and says that by submitting food photos you accept their anonymised use in marketing; opting out of marketing use means emailing support. Health consent, by contrast, is withdrawn in iOS Health settings.
steps: Goals / Application / Other, no AI row
sources: https://bitepal.app/privacy (Google Doc embed, effective Apr 29 2024: photo marketing use; Sec 3.4 HealthKit consent 'withdrawal is as easy as giving it'; marketing opt-out by contact)

lanes.summary: Sign-in offers Apple, Google or Email in one sheet. "Log out" in Settings asks once ("Sure you want to log out? Caramel will miss you a lot") and returns to the signed-out welcome with "I already have an account". Cancelled or failed sign-in and local-data clearing weren't observed.

BitePal is account-based and iPhone only (no iPad or Watch app), so signing in on a second phone should bring the account back. Restored history wasn't observed. There's no household or friends sharing; only the subscription "may be shareable" through Family Sharing.

The Today cards have designed empty states that say what goes there and offer the first action ("No fasting yet… Set a plan to start!" with "Set up fasting goal", "No fiber yet… Start logging your meals"). The Stats tab's empty state wasn't observed.
